(1) classic manifold learning methods often collapse embeddings due to the scaling of latent dimensions in observation space, (2) a simple modification of Laplacian eigenmaps, Minimally Redued Laplacian eigenmap (MR-LE), can fix this issue, and (3) MR-LE produces embeddings of comparable quality to deep learning methods.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MR-LEM algorithm can recover the latent topology of a data manifold with a single pass over data, and that it can do so without collapsing the embedding into a lower dimensional manifold.
we show that spectral manifold learning methods have been unfairly maligned and can be made competitive with deep learning methods by addressing their shortcomings.
MR-LEM can be seen as an effective alternative for learning low-dimensional representations of high-dimensional data, which can be a good starting point for further downstream learning tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spectral algorithms for learning low dimensional embeddings can be made to work well for many real-world problems if we are willing to think carefully about the geometry of the data.
the choice of embedding vector basis can have a dramatic impact on downstream learning tasks, and that simple extensions of spectral manifold learning can be surprisingly effective.
the problem of collapsed embeddings is not a bug, but a feature of data where different factors of variation have different scaling.
